<issue>
UnboundLocalError in _get_interval_distances_ratios method

#### Description

When calling methods that use `_get_interval_distances_ratios` (like `add_missing_times`, `add_missing_elevations`, `add_missing_speeds`, etc.), an `UnboundLocalError` is raised for local variables that are referenced before assignment.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import gpxpy
import datetime

# Create a simple GPX with missing time data
gpx = gpxpy.GPX()
gpx.tracks.append(gpxpy.GPXTrack())
gpx.tracks[0].segments.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackSegment())
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(latitude=13, longitude=12, time=datetime.datetime(2013, 1, 2, 12, 0)))
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(latitude=13.25, longitude=12))
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(latitude=13.5, longitude=12))
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(latitude=14, longitude=12, time=datetime.datetime(2013, 1, 2, 13, 0)))

# This will raise UnboundLocalError
gpx.add_missing_times()
```

The error occurs because variables like `distances`, `dist`, and `previous_point` are being used before they are properly initialized in the `_get_interval_distances_ratios` method.
</issue>
